public_rationale: The 2024 Foundation Model Transparency Index documented continuing opacity alongside an increase in average transparency scores from 37 in 2023 to 58 in 2024 [e1]. It assessed foundation-model developers broadly, without measuring losses to neurosymbolic research [e1]. The February 5, 2025 AlphaGeometry2 paper disclosed changes to its language model, symbolic engine, formal language, and search method [e2]. These sources establish neither the fraction of company neurosymbolic methods withheld nor substantial research losses caused by withholding, leaving the causal claim unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: The transparency audit does not isolate neurosymbolic methods or their research impact [e1].
One methodological disclosure cannot establish the overall disclosure rate or full reproducibility [e2].
The packet contains no comparison separating effects of withholding from technical difficulty or other research constraints [e1, e2].

evidence.explanation: The audit documents substantial opacity but also an improvement in average transparency from 37 to 58 out of 100. It concerns foundation-model transparency generally and does not measure lost neurosymbolic research or establish that secrecy caused such a loss.

The AlphaGeometry2 paper explicitly describes its neural-symbolic predecessor and details changes to the language model, symbolic engine, formal language, and search. This is material evidence of company disclosure, although one disclosed system cannot establish the overall disclosure rate or eliminate research losses elsewhere.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An inventory of disclosed and withheld company neurosymbolic methods through July 13, 2025, with replication and research-impact evidence showing whether withholding substantially restricted public progress after accounting for other causes.
